judged_text: add_members calls `usernames.split(",")` on `params.require(:usernames)` without asserting it is a String, so a JSON request body sending usernames as an array (the natural shape for a list of usernames) raises NoMethodError on Array#split. An admin (or an API client following the obvious JSON convention) POSTing/PUTting {usernames: ["alice","bob"]} gets a 500 instead of a 4xx; the member-add path is unusable for the JSON content-type even though the route accepts it.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff sets `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")` (see `usernames.split(",").each do |username|`). If a client sends `usernames` as an Array (e.g., JSON `{usernames: ["alice","bob"]}`), `params.require(:usernames)` will be an Array and `split` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. The diff contains no type check/coercion to prevent this.
